errors.evidence: The legend shows the Eurozone is represented by a black dashed line ('---'), not a black dotted line ('...'). The black dotted line represents Belgien (Belgium).
The starting value for Belgien (Belgium) in 1995 is approximately 130%, not 95%.
The starting value for Irland (Ireland) in 1995 is approximately 80%, not 60%.
The starting value for Italien (Italy) in 1995 is approximately 115%, not 75%.
The ending value for Belgien (Belgium) in 2025 is approximately 105%, not 120%.
The ending value for Irland (Ireland) in 2025 is approximately 40%, not 95%.
The ending value for Griechenland (Greece) in 2025 is approximately 150%, not 120%.
The ending value for Italien (Italy) in 2025 is approximately 140%, not 125%.
The value for Griechenland (Greece) in 2008 is approximately 110%, not 90%.
The value for Griechenland (Greece) in 2014 is approximately 180%, which is not 'über 200' (over 200). The line peaks above 200% in 2020, not 2014.

The prompt requires a description of how each line changes over the x-axis, but the description only details the trends for Griechenland (Greece) and Deutschland (Germany), omitting the trends for Eurozone, Belgien, Irland, Spanien, Frankreich, and Italien.
The description does not specify the tick interval for the x-axis, which is every 2 years.
The description does not specify the tick interval for the y-axis, which is every 50 percentage points.
The prompt forbids making comparisons between lines. The use of 'während' (while) introduces a comparison between the trends of Greece and Germany.
